decisions.reason: This devore decoration fabric is a trend-dependent collection item now about three years old, so it faces collection turnover risk. But it is close to the core offer and cheap to keep in stock, and the firm promises reorder continuity, so the option is kept open for now.

This transparent burnout fabric is a fashion-driven item whose value may fade as collections rotate. With no negative evidence and low holding cost within the existing warehouse and sampling setup, keeping it is the better choice.

This burnout decorative fabric overlaps with the firm's other burnout and devore variants, which raises the chance it is pruned. Absent signs of failure, its low incremental cost justifies keeping it another season.
Velour-like upholstery fabrics have longer life cycles than decorative trend fabrics and extend the firm's upholstery range. This makes the option worth holding while demand resolves.
A flame-retardant plain inbetween fabric is a functional staple with steady demand from contract and retail buyers. Its value is fairly certain, so dropping it is unlikely.
A polyester satin lining is a basic complementary product that supports made-to-measure sewing and reorder continuity. It costs little to keep and reliably adds value.
